chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Bakr, from al-Husayn al-Shaybani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Indeed, a man from your mawali considers the wealth of the Banu Umayya and their blood to be permissible, and indeed, a trust has been deposited with him by them.' He said, 'Return the trusts to their owners, even if they are Magians, for that will not be the case until our Qa'im (the Awaited Imam) arises, peace be upon him, and he makes permissible that which is permissible and forbids that which is forbidden.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning trusts to the Banu Umayya before the rise of the Mahdi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-amanat* (trusts) remaining binding on the Shia even towards their political enemies, the Banu Umayya, until the definitive rise of the Qa'im (al-Mahdi). It distinguishes between the general permissibility of their wealth and blood, which is suspended during the occultation, and the specific obligation to return deposited trusts, illustrating the juristic nuance between *halal* (permissible) and *wajib* (obligatory) in the interim period. This ruling underscores the continuity of contractual fidelity regardless of theological or political hostility, a key concept in Shia fiqh of the occultation.
